IS : 7004 - 1973

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR YEAST EXTRACT, MICROBIOLOGICAL
0. FOREWORD

GRADE

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution

on 28 August 1973, after the draft finalized by the Food Hygiene, SamplCommittee had been approved by the ing and Analysis Sectional Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Unless the ingredients used in media for microbiological work are of uniform quality, the results obtained might be erroneous and might be unreliable. Since the media used in different laboratories often differ greatly in their quality, the results of microbiological work at different Therefore, with a view to unifying the laboratories cannot be compared. practices of different laboratories dealing with microbiology and providing guidance to the indigenous manufacturers regarding the quality, it was decided to bring out a series of Indian Standard specifications for ingredients commonly used in media for microbiological work. 0.2.1 For specific purposes, any additional requirements agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. shall be as

0.3 Yeast extract is commonly used in microbiological work. It is obtained by concentrating the water soluble portion of autolyzed yeast. The autolysis should he carefully controlled to retain the naturally occurring B-complex vitamins and sufficiently high amino-acid content. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether standard is complied with, the final expressing the result of a test or analysis, The number of ance with IS : 2-1960*. rounded off value should be the same as standard. a particular requirement of this value, observed or calculated, shall be rounded off in accordsignificant places retained in the that of the specified value in this

IS : 7004 - 1973 3.3.1 The Mark. container may also be marked with the IS1 Certification

NOTE-The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control IS1 marked which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

5.2 Quality of Reagents - Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water ( see IS : 1070-1960t ) shall be employed in tests.
NOTE- ` Pure chemicals ' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the experimental results.

A-4.1 Prepare standard pyridoxine solutions containing O-125, 0'25, O-05, 1.0 and 2 pg per ml. Sterilize by heating at 1lO'C for 20 minutes. A-5. TEST SOLUTION

IS t 7004 - 1973 A-6. PREPARATION OF THE PETRI DISHES

A-6.1 Use 10 tubes each containing 20 ml of the basal medium, five of which will be required for the standard pyridoxine solutions and five tubes Melt the contents of the tubes of basal medium in for the test solutions. a boiling water-bath, and then cool to temperature of 48 to 50�C and Add 1 ml of the inoculum ( SGCA-2.I ) to maintain at this temperature. each tube and mix by rotation to distribute the yeast cells evenly throughout the medium. Pour into sterile petri dishes, 9 cm diameter, and allow to solidify. Cut 5 holes, 10 mm diameter, in medium in each petri dish using a sterile cutter. Use each petri dish for individual dilution of standard pyridoxine solutions and of the test yeast extract solutions. These are to be placed in the holes in volume of O-1 ml after which the Incubate for 18 hours holes are sealed with a drop of melted medium. at 28�C. A-7. CALCULATION FOR PYRIDOXINE CONTENT

A-7.1 Determine the mean values of the diameters of the zones of growth, Plot these values against the logarithms of the concentration of the pyndoxine standard from which the pyridoxine content of the sample can be obtained.
